text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking of pushing admission + soft-shed logic into the edge proxy instead of the central admission service. Goal: reduce tail latency and cut cross-AZ chattiness for short-lived bursts. Tradeoffs?
ashok: Interesting. Main win is fewer RTTs for token claims. But we lose a single source of truth for fairness unless proxies sync weights/fairness windows.
zoe: Would proxies keep local sketches for fairness? approximation ok, right?
ashok: Yeah, local sketches + periodic reconciliation. But abuse cases: a malicious tenant could spin many proxies to game local counts. Need hashed client identity and central abuse score fetch.
ben: Interface boundary thought: proxies should only do admission heuristics and emit a signed claim to central ledger for longer-lived reservations. Keep central service authoritative for long tails.
maria: Exactly — short-lived requests (<500ms) handled purely at edge with a small leaky-bucket + grace credits. Anything longer or cross-proxy we escalate and allocate a lease token from central.
az: (typo) — sorry, i mean infra-bot?
infra-bot: deploybot: canary proxy build v2.14 deployed to prod-edge-us-west at 1739802500 :rocket:
zoe: For fairness, what about weight drift? local algorithms will drift w.r.t central view. Maybe exchange delta snapshots every 1s? That seems heavy.
ashok: Instead push aggregated per-tenant counters every 5s, use exponential decay in central reconciler to absorb noise. Local admission uses short windows (100-200ms) so transient bursts won't be overcounted.
ben: Contract: proxy <-> central occupancy report is an append-only gRPC stream, messages: tenant_id, window_ms, tokens_used, signature. Keep it compact. Example proto sketch: 
```proto
message Occupancy { string tenant_id = 1; int32 window_ms = 2; uint64 tokens = 3; bytes sig = 4; }
service EdgeTelemetry { rpc StreamOccupancy(stream Occupancy) returns (Ack) {} }
```
zoe: How do we avoid proxies granting too many grace credits when central is under pressure? Need a backpressure hint from central: allow_globally = false/true + factor. Proxies obey factor to scale local buckets.
maria: Good call — central will broadcast an admission hint topic. Defaults: allow_globally=true, local_factor=1.0. When central sees overload, set allow_globally=false and local_factor=0.1 to force strict local shedding.
ashok: Also add an abuse flag: if central marks tenant as suspected-abuser, proxies only allow authenticated calls with stricter quotas and emit samples to abuse service.
ben: Idempotency for lease requests: include client_request_id and proxy_id so central can dedupe. Also include desired_ttl and amortize tokens for multi-chunk responses.
zoe: Ops concerns: rolling deploy of the proxy logic must be safe — proxies with new heuristics might be stricter. We need a staged rollout and a compatibility header so older central can still interpret occupancy records.
maria: Plan: 1) implement local admission with config flags off by default; 2) add telemetry stream + signature; 3) central reconciler with decay and hint publisher; 4) staged rollout with canary and gradual factor change.
ashok: Perf note: keep local admission logic C-coded in proxy path, avoid syscall heavy ops. Use preallocated ring buffers for counters.
ben: Security: signatures require each proxy to have a keypair (KMS/HSM). Rotate keys via central CA.
zoe: QA: add synthetic burst tests that validate fairness under 10k concurrent tenants and accidental clock skew.
maria: OK — I'll write a short RFC addendum with the proposed proto, hint semantics, and rollout playbook. Ping me if you want to be co-authors. :thumbsup:
